_comments: The BizApps Contracts Application — what makes this app appear in MJ Explorer at all.
WITHOUT THIS FILE the app is invisible. CodeGen auto-creates a schema-named application
(__mj_BizAppsContracts) that carries the entities, but that is a container for admin access,
not a destination: it has no nav items and no icon, so nobody finds the app by looking.
This row is the user-facing app.
DefaultNavItems is the top tab bar. Each item is ResourceType 'Custom' pointing at a
@mj-biz-apps/contracts-ng. BOTH HALVES ARE REQUIRED: metadata without a registered class
renders a dead tab, and a registered class without metadata never appears.
DefaultForNewUser is true so the app lands for new users without a per-persona grant. When
it is false you must run `mjdev apps enable <slug> <app>` or the app stays hidden even though
everything is installed correctly — a confusing failure that looks like a build problem.
The fixed UUID means a re-push against a rebuilt database UPDATES this row rather than
creating a second Application with the same name.

ONE top-level nav item on purpose: everything in this app is one section — the agreements and the machinery that bills them — so movement within it belongs on a LEFT RAIL (mj-left-nav), not on more top tabs. MJ's rule is top nav ACROSS sections, left nav WITHIN one. Additional top tabs are expected later for genuinely separate areas (settings and the like), which is exactly what this slot is for.

fields.Name: Contracts
fields.Description: The agreement envelope — commitment, term structure, escalation, renewal and the billing event. Contracts decides what is owed and when; orders remains the only place anyone is billed.
